summary: Created src/menu/renderer.ts with renderMenu(config: MenuConfig): void.

Clears screen via clearScreen(), renders banner lines in cyan, version in dim, category headers bold with optional dim sub-project versions, commands with [key] label format, [h] Help [q] Quit footer, and Choose: prompt (no trailing newline).
Commands with hidden: true or key: null are excluded from the interactive menu.
Category insertion order preserved based on first command occurrence.

comments.note: src/menu/renderer.ts: the footer uses two separate C.dim() calls ([h] Help and [q] Quit) rather than wrapping both in a single call. This is a minor style choice; a single C.dim('[h] Help  [q] Quit') would also work. No behavioral difference.

src/menu/renderer.ts: commands are filtered to non-hidden and key !== null, but 'helpHidden' commands are still shown in the interactive menu. This is intentional (helpHidden only suppresses help output), but the distinction is subtle and worth documenting in the constraints if it isn't already.

tests/menu/renderer.test.ts, makeConfig(): workspaceRoot defaults to '/tmp/test' (Unix-specific path). On Windows this resolves unexpectedly. Prefer os.tmpdir() from 'node:os' for cross-platform test fixtures. Low risk for current usage since workspaceRoot is not exercised by renderer.test.ts, but worth standardising across all test helpers.

src/menu/renderer.ts, footer: the two dim calls (`C.dim('[h] Help')` + double space + `C.dim('[q] Quit')`) leave the separator space unstyled (outside both dim wrappers). A single `C.dim('[h] Help  [q] Quit')` would dim-style the separator too. Cosmetically indistinguishable in any terminal; no action required unless strict ANSI output assertion tests are added in future.

[documentation-forward] The hidden vs helpHidden command flag distinction is subtle and not currently documented in the library README or API reference. Add a section (or table) explaining: `hidden: true` — command is excluded from both the interactive menu and help output; `helpHidden: true` — command is excluded from help output only, still appears in the interactive menu; `key: null` — command has no single-character key and is therefore only accessible via direct CLI invocation (excluded from the interactive menu but may appear in help). This is the primary source of confusion for consumers adding commands to the library.
